help.intro: Sooner or later everyone living in Germany needs a doctor, and the visit follows a fixed script: saying what hurts and since when, hearing the diagnosis, getting a prescription, going to the pharmacy. The vocabulary sits in three groups. Complaints: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen / Bauchschmerzen / Halsschmerzen / Fieber / Husten / Schnupfen / eine Erkältung; Mein Bein tut weh. The people and places: der Arzt / die Ärztin, die Praxis, die Apotheke, das Krankenhaus. The things: das Rezept (prescription), das Medikament, die Tablette, die Krankenkasse (health insurance), die Versichertenkarte. Two grammar chunks carry the dialogue: seit + dative for how long (seit drei Tagen) and Sie müssen / Sie sollten for the doctor's advice.
help.tips[0].text: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen / Fieber / Husten / eine Erkältung. Mein Rücken tut weh. Ich bin krank / müde / erkältet. Mir ist schlecht (I feel sick) — dative!
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I've had a sore throat and a temperature for three days.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: I feel sick and I'm cold.
help.tips[0].check.q: ____ ist schlecht. Ich muss mich kurz hinlegen.
help.tips[0].check.why: Feeling sick takes the dative: Mir ist schlecht. 'Ich bin schlecht' would mean you are bad at something, or a bad person.
help.tips[1].text: seit gestern, seit drei Tagen, seit einer Woche, seit Montag — with the present tense: Ich habe seit gestern Fieber.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Since when have you had the pain? – For two days.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: I've had a sore throat since Monday.
help.tips[1].check.why: seit takes the dative, and the dative plural adds -n: seit zwei Monaten.
help.tips[1].visual.marks[0].label: and still ill
help.tips[2].title: The doctor's side
help.tips[2].text: Was fehlt Ihnen? / Wo tut es weh? (what's wrong / where does it hurt) — Sie müssen im Bett bleiben. Sie sollten viel trinken. Ich schreibe Ihnen ein Rezept. Nehmen Sie die Tabletten dreimal täglich.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: You have a cold. You must drink a lot and stay in bed.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Where does it hurt? – Here, in my stomach.
help.tips[2].check.why: Pain is wehtun: Es tut weh, Wo tut es weh?
help.tips[3].text: The doctor's surgery (Praxis) gives you a prescription (Rezept); the pharmacy (Apotheke) gives you the medicine. Three nouns, one story — and Rezept is also a cooking recipe.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: With the prescription I go to the pharmacy.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: The doctor gives me a prescription, and at the pharmacy I get the tablets.
help.tips[3].trap: die Apotheke is a pharmacy (medicines), die Drogerie sells toiletries. And der Arzt is a doctor of medicine; a Doktor may be any PhD.
help.tips[3].check.q: Der Arzt hat dir ein Rezept gegeben. Die Tabletten bekommst du in der ____.
help.tips[3].check.why: Prescriptions are filled at the Apotheke. The Drogerie sells toiletries, and the Praxis is where the doctor works.
help.remember[0]: haben + …schmerzen / tut weh / sein + krank: the three ways to complain.
help.remember[1]: seit + dative + present tense = how long it has been going on.
help.context.en: Hello, what's the matter? – I've had a cough and headaches for four days, and I'm always cold. – Do you have a temperature? – Yes, 38.5. – You have a cold. I'll write you a prescription; take the tablets twice a day and stay at home for three days. – Thank you, doctor.
help.mistakes[0].why: Feeling sick takes the dative: mir ist schlecht.
help.mistakes[1].why: seit takes the dative plural: Tagen.
help.mistakes[2].why: Prescriptions are filled at the Apotheke.
help.hook: Say what hurts, since when, and understand what the doctor tells you. That's a whole visit to the doctor in German.
sentences[0].english: I have a headache and take a pill.
sentences[0].why: Aches are plural compounds: Kopf + -schmerzen = Kopfschmerzen.
sentences[1].english: My leg hurts, I cannot walk.
sentences[1].why: das Bein — 'leg'; you need it for laufen, walking.
sentences[2].why: der Arzt — the doctor; untersuchen is to examine.
sentences[3].english: I buy the medicine at the pharmacy.
sentences[3].why: die Apotheke — the pharmacy; medicines come from there, not the Drogerie.
sentences[4].english: I am ill and stay in bed.
sentences[4].why: krank — 'ill'; the root of Krankenhaus and Krankenversicherung.
sentences[5].english: I have a stomach ache — too much chocolate!
sentences[6].english: My throat hurts, I can hardly speak.
sentences[6].why: der Hals — neck and throat in one word.
sentences[7].english: I have a temperature of 39 — I have a fever.
sentences[7].why: das Fieber — fever; German 'has' it: Fieber haben.
sentences[8].english: The doctor gives me a prescription for tablets.
sentences[8].why: das Rezept — both prescription and recipe in German.
sentences[9].english: I take a medicine for the pain.
sentences[9].why: das Medikament — medicine; gegen says what it fights.
sentences[10].english: My eyes hurt — I sit at the computer too long.
sentences[10].why: das Auge → die Augen — the -n plural; tun is plural to match.
sentences[11].english: I can't hear well, my ears hurt.
sentences[11].why: das Ohr → die Ohren — the -en plural.
sentences[12].english: I've hurt my hand and can't write.
sentences[12].why: die Hand — with verletzen German says mir … die Hand, not 'my hand'.
sentences[13].sentence: Ich habe eine ____ und muss niesen. (a cold)
sentences[13].english: I have a cold and have to sneeze.
sentences[13].why: die Erkältung — from kalt: the 'being-colded'; -ung words are always die.
sentences[14].english: My head hurts — I slept too little.
sentences[14].why: der Kopf — 'head'; one thing hurts, so tut.
sentences[15].english: I've had a sore throat for two days and can hardly swallow.
sentences[16].english: I take the prescription to the pharmacy.
sentences[16].why: das Rezept — the doctor's note the pharmacy needs; mit dem shows its dative.
sentences[17].english: I broke my leg playing football.
sentences[17].why: das Bein — broken bones go mir … das Bein gebrochen, dative person + article.
sentences[18].english: My son has a fever, so I'm phoning the doctor's surgery.
sentences[18].why: die Praxis — the doctor's surgery/office, where you call for a Termin.
